text.p: Malaysia's power utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd on Monday reported net profit of 511 million ringgit ($204 million) in the six months to end-February, up 36 percent from 370 million ringgit in the year-ago period.
The profit figure, which was boosted by a foreign exchange gain, was above market expectations of around 500 million ringgit for the period ended February 28, analysts said.
Net earnings per share rose to 17 cents from 12 cents, while turnover increased to 4.68 billion ringgit from 3.72 billion.

Tenaga said in its financial statement that the improvement in its profit was mainly due to higher electricity sales, a foreign exchange gain and a tariff adjustment of 8 percent, effective from March 1, 1996. The company said it also saw demand growth of 13.5 percent in the six-month period.
"The results are quite satisfactory. Net profit is slightly above expectations," said Haizan Johari, investment manager at KL Mutual Fund Bhd.
However, analysts said Tenaga's profit increase was largely helped by a big foreign exchange gain.
